clips.title: The Explore → Plan → Code → Commit workflow in Claude Code
clips.why: Anthropic's own short version of the habit Nova is built on: research, then a plan with success criteria, and only then code.
look: Exploring comes before planning, and planning before code. Nova's readiness check and grill sit at the very front of the same order.
Success criteria are decided while planning, not after the code. That is our definition of done and QA plan.
A separate reviewer before pushing: you will meet Nova's fresh-eyes reviewers two lessons from now.
clips.after: In a person's session this is a habit; in Nova it is a schema the planner must fill and a button the requester must press.

clips.title: Definition of Done vs Acceptance Criteria: What's the Difference?
clips.channel: Mountain Goat Software: Agile & Scrum Mastery
clips.why: Mike Cohn separates the two words cleanly, and it helps to know that our plan's "definition of done" field is what Scrum calls acceptance criteria.
look: Acceptance criteria are specific to one story. Our definition_of_done belongs to one ticket, so it is this kind.
The examples of acceptance criteria are written as what a user can do and see, like our user_sees lines.
A team-wide definition of done (tests pass, reviewed, and so on) also exists for us: it is the ready gate a later lesson builds.
clips.after: Nova writes the ticket-specific part in the plan, and the platform enforces the team-wide part on every PR.

clips.title: Spec-Driven Development: AI Assisted Coding Explained
clips.why: A clear picture of writing the spec first and letting the AI work from it, instead of prompting and hoping.
look: The spec is written and reviewed before the code, by a person.
The code is then checked against the spec, which is how our QA checks are used later.
Compare it with "vibe coding" from the earlier part of the video: no agreed target, so no way to say it is done.
clips.after: Nova's plan is a small spec with a fixed shape, and the requester's Approve is the review step.

practice.q: Which QA check for RH-1234 is written the way the plan wants?

options.text: "The EmptyCard component renders with className empty-card"
options.why: A class name says how the code works, not what the user sees. It can stay right while the screen is wrong.

options.text: "With no projects, the table shows the text No projects yet"
options.why: It says what a user sees, and a test can read the visible text.
A broken build can pass this. A check must fail when the ticket is not done.

practice.q: Convert the plan schema for the planner so fields with a default are optional for the model, and the SDK accepts the draft.
practice.why: Input mode describes what the model may send, so edge_case with its default is optional. Output mode would make it required.

practice.q: The SDK accepted the planner's JSON. Why does the harness still run Plan.safeParse?

options.text: To turn the JSON into a string for the Slack app
options.why: Parsing goes the other way: it turns unknown JSON into a typed plan.

options.text: Because superRefine rules, like the edge-case rule, are not in the JSON Schema the SDK used
options.why: Only zod runs them. The issues it finds go back to the planner.

options.text: Because the SDK accepts any JSON, whatever the schema
options.why: The SDK does check the shape. It just cannot check rules it never received.

practice.q: Nova estimated 70 minutes for RH-1234. At minute 95 it is still building. What happens?

options.text: The run is stopped and the ticket goes back
options.why: The estimate is never a limit. Stopping would throw away work in the middle.

options.text: Nova posts a short check-in and keeps working unless someone says stop
options.why: The estimate is measured and drives check-ins. A person decides whether to stop.

options.text: The plan is sent back to the planner to raise the estimate
options.why: The plan was approved. The estimate is a guess, and being wrong is information, not an error.

practice.q: Put RH-1234's way from ticket to approved plan in order.
items: The readiness check says ready, size small, so there is no grill
The planner writes plan v1 on a lite VM and the harness checks it with safeParse
The QA agent signs the QA plan, and the plan is posted in Jira and Slack
You press Change and write that a filter with no match must say No results
Nova posts plan v2, you press Approve, and the workflow claims a full VM
practice.why: Questions come before the plan, code checks come before people see it, and money is spent only after Approve.
